argument:
The bear properly identifies weakening conversion, but the scale matters: annual cash FCF remained $66.987bn despite almost-doubled capex, and CFO rose from $136.162bn to $182.935bn. That is observed internal funding growth rather than merely a balance-sheet reserve financing losses. The annual cash measure also supports actual shareholder returns, while its lease and noncash limits remain explicit.

At 30.63x OpenAI-adjusted FY earnings, 22% adjusted EPS growth provides a substantive compounding basis without relying on investment gains. Future growth is not guaranteed and incremental cloud returns matter, but the 6.5% FCF decline does not negate strongly positive cash and liquidity. The bullish case is funded profitable expansion earning its premium over time; overbought positioning argues for deliberate entry rather than abandoning that evidence.
key_points: CFO grew materially while cash FCF remained strongly positive.
Adjusted EPS growth supplies a premium-compounding basis.
Lease burdens and weaker conversion remain explicit.
rebuttal_to_previous: The FCF decline is real, but $66.987bn remaining after $115.948bn cash PP&E demonstrates funded expansion. Rising CFO and22% adjusted EPS growth support productive operating compounding; I do not claim all lease/noncash demands are included or that the premium must persist.
